methodology: The taxonomy draws on the published topics of major AI conferences. Research maturity and open questions are editorial syntheses, not official conference ratings or quantitative measurements.

layers.A: Mathematical foundations of learning from finite data, optimization, and causal identification.
layers.B: Model structures for representing observations, distributions, and knowledge.
layers.C: Interpreting visual, audio, language, and structured observations.
layers.D: Reasoning, planning, deciding, and acting in environments.
layers.E: Evaluating, explaining, and safeguarding AI behavior.
layers.F: Efficient, privacy-preserving, and large-scale AI computation.
layers.G: Scientific discovery, physical modeling, and insights from brains and cognition.

A1.progress: PAC learning, generalization bounds, and sample complexity have established theoretical foundations; understanding modern deep networks remains an active research area.
questions: How can we derive tight generalization bounds for overparameterized networks?
What guarantees are possible for out-of-distribution and interactive data?
How should the statistical complexity of learned representations be measured?

A2.progress: SGD, Adam, and related optimizers are widely used; the dynamics and efficiency of large-scale nonconvex training remain active topics.
questions: What theory can explain optimization in large nonconvex models?
How can training stability, computation, and optimality be balanced?
Under what conditions does stochastic optimization converge on heterogeneous data?

A3.progress: Supervised and unsupervised learning have mature toolkits; self-supervised, active, and weak supervision continue to expand.
questions: How can learning depend less on human annotations?
How should noise and bias in weak supervision be addressed?
How can the most informative samples be selected efficiently?

A4.progress: Large-scale pretraining has improved transfer, but continual adaptation, representation stability, and identifiability remain challenging.
questions: Which invariant factors can be shared across tasks?
How can catastrophic forgetting be reduced during continual learning?
When can transferability of a representation be established?

A5.progress: Probabilistic modeling and MCMC have mature foundations; scalable inference for complex latent, non-Gaussian, and neural models remains active.
questions: How can high-dimensional posterior approximation balance speed and accuracy?
Is uncertainty reliable under model misspecification?
How can inference be performed for implicit generative processes?

A6.progress: Potential-outcome and graphical identification theories are established; high-dimensional confounding, interference, spatial-temporal causality, and causal representations remain active.
questions: What can be concluded when observational data do not identify a causal effect?
How do interference and distribution shift affect causal estimands?
What causal meaning can be assigned to neural representations?

B1.progress: Transformers, CNNs, and state-space neural networks are widely studied; efficiency, long-context processing, and inductive bias remain central.
questions: Which architectures capture long-range dependencies most efficiently?
How can expressiveness and interpretability be balanced?
How can training and inference costs be reduced?

B2.progress: Diffusion, flow matching, and autoregressive generation have made major advances; controllability, probabilistic evaluation, and long-horizon consistency remain open.
questions: Does realistic generation imply accurate physical world dynamics?
How should uncertainty in generated outcomes be quantified?
How can fine-grained conditional control be achieved?

B3.progress: GNNs and graph structure-learning tools are increasingly capable; long-range interactions, transferability, and structural uncertainty remain challenges.
questions: How can message passing capture long-range dependencies?
How can an unknown graph structure be learned efficiently?
How should probabilistic graphical inference connect with GNNs?

B4.progress: General-purpose pretraining and adaptation have broadened model capabilities; cross-task reliability, data efficiency, and evaluation are increasingly important.
questions: What transferable knowledge does pretraining acquire?
Do scaling laws generalize across modalities and data regimes?
How can genuine generalization be measured?

B5.progress: Symbolic logic and automated reasoning have established foundations; combining neural representations with verifiable symbolic reasoning remains exploratory.
questions: How can continuous neural representations be connected to discrete rules?
How can reasoning remain reliable with uncertain knowledge?
How can symbolic knowledge be learned and updated automatically?

C1.progress: 2D recognition and detection have mature toolkits; 3D understanding, dynamic scenes, and physical spatial reasoning remain active.
questions: How can real 3D structure be inferred from limited viewpoints?
How should models handle occlusion and changing environments?
How can videos maintain spatiotemporal consistency?

C2.progress: Language pretraining has made substantial advances; semantic reliability, long-document comprehension, and multilingual access remain important.
questions: How can language understanding be distinguished from memorization?
Can long-context systems reason consistently?
How can low-resource languages receive equitable capabilities?

C3.progress: Speech recognition and synthesis are widely deployed; complex soundscapes, cross-lingual transfer, and robustness remain open.
questions: How can speech separation and recognition improve under noise?
How can the causal structure of acoustic events be learned?
How can audio be integrated reliably with other modalities?

C4.progress: Vision-language and audiovisual models are advancing rapidly; cross-modal grounding and compositional reasoning remain difficult.
questions: How can multiple modalities represent the same physical entities?
Does cross-modal alignment support causal inference?
How can reasoning remain reliable when a modality is missing?

C5.progress: Search and recommendation are highly developed in industry; feedback loops, selection bias, and long-term impact remain difficult to evaluate.
questions: How do recommendation exposures change the observed data distribution?
How can feedback-loop bias be avoided?
How can knowledge bases be updated and verified continuously?

C6.progress: Classical statistical models are mature; time-series foundation models, nonstationary generalization, and high-dimensional spatiotemporal learning remain active.
questions: How can predictive reliability be preserved under nonstationarity?
How should irregular sampling and missingness be modeled?
How should uncertainty in long-range forecasting be represented?

D1.progress: Classical search, logic, and planning are mature; verifiable multistep reasoning in dynamic settings remains difficult.
questions: How should symbolic search be combined with neural reasoning?
How can plans be made under uncertainty and partial observability?
How can long reasoning chains be verified?

D2.progress: Classical MDP and control theories are mature, and deep RL is widely studied; sample efficiency, safety, and long-term generalization remain priorities.
questions: How can the cost of real-world interaction be reduced?
How can offline data support safe policy improvement?
How can policy transfer into new environments be validated?

D3.progress: Tool use and computer-interaction capabilities are improving rapidly; long-term reliability, memory, and multi-agent coordination remain weak points.
questions: How can errors during long tasks be detected and repaired?
How can multiple agents coordinate without unstable behavior?
How should task capabilities and associated risks be evaluated?

D4.progress: Performance in controlled environments is improving, but complex household tasks and real-world deployment still show substantial gaps.
questions: How can policies learned in simulation transfer safely?
How can contact-rich manipulation be executed reliably?
How can errors be prevented from accumulating in long tasks?

D5.progress: Environment dynamics and action-conditioned generation are active areas; long-horizon prediction, consistency, and planning utility lack unified evaluation.
questions: Does realistic generation reflect accurate dynamics?
How can long-horizon counterfactual predictions be evaluated?
What kinds of world models are most useful for planning?

E1.progress: Robustness, calibration, and explanation methods are diverse; mechanistic validity, OOD reliability, and safety constraints remain challenging.
questions: How can uncertainty estimates remain valid under distribution shift?
Do explanations capture correlations or causal mechanisms?
How can model safety be verified systematically?

E2.progress: Model capabilities change faster than some benchmarks; data contamination, experimental design, and evaluation validity are increasingly important.
questions: How can genuine ability be measured when benchmarks saturate?
Do evaluation metrics match real-world objectives?
How can data contamination and spurious progress be prevented?

E3.progress: Human-AI interaction and governance are maturing; fairness, transparency, and accountability depend heavily on context.
questions: How should long-term outcomes of human-AI collaboration be evaluated?
How should competing stakeholder interests be balanced?
How can AI decisions remain open to societal oversight?

F1.progress: GPU training, quantization, and inference optimization have mature practical methods and remain active; energy and resource constraints continue to evolve.
questions: How can models be compressed while preserving quality?
How can latency be reduced for long-context and real-time inference?
How can complex models be deployed on resource-limited devices?

F2.progress: Federated learning and differential privacy have established theory and deployments; privacy–utility tradeoffs and heterogeneous clients remain difficult.
questions: How does the privacy budget affect utility in practice?
How can heterogeneous client data be used fairly?
How can distributed training resist attacks?

G1.progress: Applications in proteins, materials, climate, and scientific simulation are expanding; validation, extrapolation, and closed-loop discovery remain central challenges.
questions: How can physical laws be integrated with data-driven learning?
How can proposed scientific discoveries be verified experimentally?
How can reliable extrapolation be maintained with scarce scientific data?

G2.progress: Computational neuroscience and cognitive modeling increasingly intersect with AI; mapping biological mechanisms to verifiable AI designs remains contested.
questions: Which neural mechanisms are useful as algorithmic inspiration?
How do neural and behavioral mechanisms correspond to model computations?
How can cognitive capabilities be tested causally?

P1.description: Models can fail on unseen tasks, environments, or data distributions.
P1.question: Which invariances genuinely support transfer across environments?

P2.description: Annotation, simulation, interaction, and experimental data can be costly.
P2.question: How can models learn from fewer but more informative examples?

P3.description: Computational costs constrain high-dimensional optimization, inference, and deployment.
P3.question: How can precision and speed be balanced under hard resource limits?

P4.description: Reported probabilities or confidence scores do not always match actual error risk.
P4.question: How can uncertainty estimates remain reliable as data structures change?

P5.description: Errors can propagate through extended prediction and action sequences.
P5.question: How can deviations in long trajectories be detected and corrected?

P6.description: Statistical association does not guarantee correct predictions under intervention.
P6.question: How can testable mechanisms and counterfactual models be established?

P7.description: Learned representations may lack stable semantics or compositional structure.
P7.question: Which representations support compositional generalization?

P8.description: Changing tasks and environments can degrade performance or cause forgetting.
P8.question: When should a model adapt, and how can catastrophic forgetting be avoided?

P9.description: Benchmarks may not reflect real abilities, and research results may be hard to reproduce.
P9.question: How can tests achieve construct validity and reproducibility?

P10.description: Multiple agents, competing goals, and real-world deployment introduce new risks.
P10.question: How can conflicting objectives be reconciled and safety boundaries tested?

P11.description: Visually plausible outputs are not necessarily physically feasible.
P11.question: How can dynamics constrained by physical laws be learned from observations?

P12.description: Knowledge can become stale, and multistep reasoning can contain hidden errors.
P12.question: How can external knowledge and multistep reasoning be validated?
